task_and_output: [1] Electrophysiology: whole-cell recordings of membrane potential of HSN, VS1-2 and OGIN (optic-glomerulus small-object) cells in tethered flying flies during spontaneous flight saccades (measured as left-right wingbeat amplitude difference); output: saccade-related potentials (SRPs) in mV and their timing relative to wing/head motion. [2] Same preparation, 47 identified HS/VS cells of 9 types; output: SRP amplitude per cell type vs. that cell's yaw visual sensitivity; plus head-movement behaviour (magnetic tether, 350 Hz video) and silencing of HS/VS (Kir2.1) to show HS/VS drive gaze-stabilising head yaw. [3] Recordings from motion-sensitive cells during three turn types (looming-evoked, spontaneous, optomotor turns to brief motion pulses); output: presence/absence of motor-related signals. [4] Retinal muscle movement: photoreceptor displacement (deg), optokinetic smooth tracking and retinal saccades; receptive-field shift of LC14 cells; HS/VS responses to retinal micro-saccades. [5] HS-cell recordings (HSN/HSE/HSS) during looming-evoked and spontaneous saccades combined with panoramic horizontal motion; output: hyperpolarisation and suppression of motion responses. [6] HS cells in walking flies encode angular and translational walking velocity independently of vision. [7] Volumetric imaging of LC (lobula columnar) populations; output: tuning and gain of small-object detectors across saccades. [8] Behavioural model: 'virtual fly' steering (wing response) to mixtures of visual patterns combined via different internal models, compared with magnetically tethered flies. [9] Multi-object tracker: Kalman box predictions are warped by a per-frame affine image registration (camera motion compensation) before IoU association; output MOT boxes and IDs.
data_and_independent_videos: No natural-video datasets in [1]-[8]: all are laboratory stimuli on LED arenas or screens (gratings, uniform illumination, moving spots/bars, looming discs). [1]: 10 HSN cells (5 blinded flies), 21 VS1-2 cells, 21 OGIN cells. [2]: 55 cells recorded, 47 identified HS/VS cells; number of flies in behaviour not stated in text. [3]: n not verified [uncertain]. [4]: 6 LC14 cells for receptive-field shift; 12 HS/VS cells for retinal saccade responses. [5]: 13 flies ipsilateral looming (11 classified cells), 13 flies contralateral looming, 16 cells with known subtype (5 HSN, 7 HSE, 4 HSS). [6], [7], [8]: counts not extracted [uncertain]. No train/test split concept applies to [1]-[7]; [8] fits simple models to single-stimulus responses and tests on mixtures [uncertain]. [9]: MOT17 validation = second half of each of the 7 MOT17 train sequences, detector trained on first halves (same videos, different frames).
target_size_and_input_resolution: Biology: real compound eye (~700-750 ommatidia per eye in Drosophila, interommatidial spacing ~5 deg); stimuli are wide-field gratings (HS/VS) or small spots/bars (OGIN, LC). [4]: retina displaced up to ~15 deg peak-to-peak (~3 inter-photoreceptor spacings) under optogenetic drive; spontaneous retinal saccades usually <1 deg (up to ~5 deg in darkness; mean 2.6 +- 1.6 deg in darkness vs 0.9 +- 0.4 deg with grating, Fig. 4c); LC14 receptive fields ~50 deg wide shifted by the measured 5.7 deg pseudopupil displacement (Fig. 2g-h). Target sizes in [1]/[7] not extracted [uncertain]. [9]: full-resolution MOT17 frames (1920x1080 or 640x480), pedestrians.
frame_rate_and_camera_motion: Tethered flight, so real body rotation absent; saccades are intended (fictive) turns. Tethered saccades last ~300-500 ms vs 50-150 ms in free flight ([1]). Head video 350 Hz ([2]). Stimulus arenas typically refresh far above 30 Hz [uncertain: exact rates not extracted]. Self-motion during recordings: head and retina may move; in [5] the head was fixed. [9]: MOT17 at 14-30 fps with moving (vehicle/handheld) and static cameras.

metrics_and_numbers: [1] Kim 2015 (PMC6327952): HSN membrane potential correlates with left-right wingbeat difference, t(9) = 10.34, P = 1e-6; persists in blinded flies (n = 5). HSN SRP with uniform screen: -3.5 mV (leftward saccades), +1.8 mV (rightward). During grating motion leftward SRP grows to -5.5 mV (P = 0.004) against an ongoing +6.4 mV visual depolarisation (difference n.s., P = 0.258), i.e. near-complete but partial cancellation; rightward +2.9 mV vs -3.0 mV visual response (n.s.). VS1-2 (n = 21): weak bidirectional effects, t(20) = 3.09, P = 0.006. OGIN (n = 21): both saccade directions hyperpolarise, -4.4 mV vs +5.4 mV visual response (rightward spot), -4.0 mV vs +5.9 mV (leftward spot); SRPs last ~400-500 ms. Timing: HSN visual latency 24 ms (preferred) / 30 ms (null); HSN SRPs start 25-39 ms BEFORE saccade onset and >=21 ms before wing motion; OGIN SRP 68-69 ms after wingbeat change; head follows wings by ~20 ms (Results, figures on SRP timing). [2] Kim 2017 (PMC6320683): Kir2.1 in HS/VS reduces depolarising visual responses to ~25% of wild type and dampens head optomotor yaw by ~50% at 180 deg/s (Fig. 2; p = 0.0028/0.0013 and 0.0059/0.0010 for two lines). Yaw visual responses: HS 5.6 +- 0.7 mV, VS4-6 2.5 +- 0.4 mV, VS1-3 0.8 +- 0.4 mV (Fig. 4). SRP magnitude across 9 cell types anticorrelated with yaw sensitivity: r = -0.90, p = 0.003 (with stimulus) and r = -0.90, p = 0.002 (blank screen); no correlation for pitch or roll (Figs. 5-6). SRP vs pre-saccadic potential (Fig. 7): HS slope -0.29, zero-crossing -60 mV (r = -0.97); VS4-6 slope -0.27, -58 mV (r = -0.84); VS1-3 slope -0.18, -47 mV (r = -0.98) - consistent with tuned inhibitory input to HS/VS4-6 and weaker shunting to VS1-3. During yaw saccades the head turns WITH the body (anti-stabilising), consistent with suppression of the HS-driven head reflex (Fig. 3). [3] Fenk 2021 (abstract): motor-related signals present for looming-evoked and spontaneous turns, weak or non-existent for optomotor turns to brief unidirectional motion pulses; numbers not verified [uncertain]. [4] Fenk 2022 (PMC10103069): retina displacement ~15 deg peak-to-peak (Fig. 1d-e); LC14 receptive fields shift by 5.7 deg with retina (6/6 cells, Fig. 2g-h); retinal saccade peak velocity >600 deg/s, counter-saccades >140 deg/s (Ext. Data Fig. 4); initial retinal speed ~3 deg/s for 15 deg/s gratings (implied gain ~0.2, computed by us, Ext. Data Fig. 5); HS/VS respond to sub-1 deg retinal movements, sometimes near full dynamic range (N = 12, Ext. Data Fig. 8); weak opposite-sign response in darkness 'may represent an efference copy' (Ext. Data Fig. 8 legend). [5] Fischer & Schnell 2022 (PMC9523382): looming-evoked saccades hyperpolarise only a subset of HS cells (HPspont, p = 0.001, Fig. 2; HPcontra, p = 5e-6, Fig. 4); subtype predicts the spontaneous-saccade response better than saccade amplitude (rho = 0.68, p = 0.002 vs rho = 0.4, p = 0.10, Fig. 3; hyperpolarisation mostly in HSN, HSS biphasic); looming alone suppresses clockwise-motion responses even without flight (p = 1.6e-3), additional saccade-related reduction in HPspont (p = 0.031) (Fig. 5). [6] Fujiwara 2017: HS cells encode angular and translational walking velocity non-visually; nonvisual and visual selectivity cooperate only when visual input matches expected self-motion (abstract; i.e. in walking the motor signal ADDS to expected reafference rather than cancelling it). [7] Turner 2022: small-object LC neurons have gain reduced during saccades by a motor-related and a rotational-visual signal, restored between saccades (abstract; magnitudes not extracted [uncertain]). [9] BoT-SORT Table 1 (MOT17 val, TrackEval): ByteTrack baseline HOTA 67.88, IDF1 79.77, MOTA 77.66; +KF state 68.12 / 79.89 / 77.67; +CMC 69.06 / 81.51 / 78.31 (CMC adds +0.94 HOTA, +1.62 IDF1); +Pred 69.11; +ReID 69.17.

mechanism_summary: Published mechanism: during a VOLUNTARY, course-changing body turn (saccade), an internally generated motor-related signal arrives at specific wide-field optic-flow cells (HSN, HS, VS4-6) with the opposite sign of the visual response that the turn would cause, starting 25-39 ms before the saccade, scaled per cell type to that cell's yaw sensitivity (r = -0.90) and roughly matching but not fully cancelling the visual response (-5.5 mV vs +6.4 mV). Its function is to prevent the stabilising reflexes (head yaw, optomotor steering) driven by HS/VS from fighting the intended turn. It is absent during course-stabilising turns (Fenk 2021): reafference from stabilising movements is NOT cancelled. It acts on only a subset of HS cells and is mixed with stimulus-driven suppression (Fischer & Schnell 2022). Object-detecting LC cells are handled differently: their gain is turned down during saccades and restored between them (Turner 2022), i.e. saccadic suppression/gating, not subtraction. In walking (Fujiwara 2017) the motor signal in HS cells has the same sign as expected flow (an internal self-motion estimate, not a canceller). The fly also moves its retina under the lens: receptive fields shift with the retina (5.7 deg), small retinal saccades strongly drive HS/VS, and no explicit state remapping is described - the network simply sees the shifted image. Nothing in [1]-[7] shows remapping of neuron state into new retinal coordinates; that concept comes from primate predictive remapping and is not reported for Drosophila. Engineering analogue: BoT-SORT warps track predictions (not detector features) by an estimated affine camera motion, +0.94 HOTA on MOT17 val (single run). Proposed modification for our case (ours, not published): treat a crop jump/rescale as a 'saccade' -> gate (suppress) motion readout for a short window, and treat small smooth crop following as 'course-stabilising' -> no cancellation; for residual object motion use a forward-model subtraction of the stock-FlyVis response to the predicted crop motion of a static scene.
transfer_limits: 1) Our crop motion is KNOWN exactly (we set crop centre and scale), whereas the fly must predict its own motion; the problem is therefore image-coordinate bookkeeping, which resampling or re-rendering solves exactly, not prediction - the biological solution (an approximate, partial, per-cell-type cancelling current) is strictly weaker than what is available to us. 2) Biology cancels only rotation (yaw) in a few wide-field cell types; our crop motion includes translation and RESCALING (square max(2x long side, 64 px) changes size every frame), which produces expansion/contraction flow that HS/VS-like yaw cancellation does not address; no Drosophila evidence for scale efference copy. 3) Timing: fly saccades are 50-150 ms (free) with HS latencies 24-30 ms and SRPs leading by 25-39 ms; at 30 Hz one frame is 33 ms, so a crop jump is a single-frame step - the fly's continuous-time anticipatory timing has no counterpart, and FlyVis temporal filters (trained on Sintel at its integration dt) see a frame step as a strong transient regardless. 4) Magnitudes: crop shifts of several hexals per frame at 721 hexals, targets ~9.37 x 12.06 lattice steps, are far above retinal micro-saccades (<1 deg ~ 0.2 ommatidia) and comparable to optogenetic maximum (~3 spacings); yet even <1 deg retinal saccades drove HS/VS near full range - so crop motion will dominate motion-cell outputs unless removed. 5) Project evidence: state remapping (fly_efference_eye_v1: per-cell-type barycentric transfer of state to new crop coordinates plus re-rendered past stimulus) confirmed geometry (false object transfer 0.05-0.07 of eye path vs 0.40-0.62 for output-side efference copy) but failed the magnitude gate (T3 length 0.58 < 0.6; T4 12.9 px > 12; scene-dependent gain 2-2.5x); v2 (transfer of initial response + accumulated calibration) failed T1 and was worse than legacy on 6/6 images; DIS optical flow on the same stabilised crops passed with large margin (T4 0.3 px). Literature therefore cannot rescue remapping by biological analogy: the biology does not remap state. 6) Fenk 2021 implies smooth, stabilising gaze following should NOT be cancelled; our crop follows the track prediction (stabilising), so cancelling reafference there contradicts the biological principle - but in our setting the crop motion is not useful information for the readout either. 7) Environment: YOLO/ByteTrack/MASA already handle global camera motion only partially (ByteTrack has no CMC; BoT-SORT-style CMC is an external tracker change, not a FlyVis node, and per AGENTS.md must be separated as the 'without fly' variant). 8) Literature is about rejecting self-induced motion, not about finding the previous target among similar neighbours or refusing - it does not address Z13's failure (localisation and confidence selection).
research_questions_addressed: Q3 (direct evidence on the regime): establishes that the fly's self-motion cancellation is rotation-only, cell-type-specific, partial, context-dependent (course-changing only) and timed around 50-500 ms saccades - none tested at 30 Hz frame steps, with rescaling, or with natural video; transfer to our moving and rescaling crop is by design analogy only. Q2 (caution on the state-transfer node): no Drosophila evidence for remapping neuron state into new eye coordinates; the published mechanisms are subtraction at specific output cells and gain gating of feature detectors; combined with the project's failed v1/v2 remapping, this argues against investing further in state remapping as the FlyVis modernisation. Q5 (design analogy for a minimal, cheap check): saccadic gain gating of the readout is a one-parameter node that can be checked on existing gates without training. Q1 and Q4: not addressed (no exemplar, distractor or refusal mechanism).
candidate_node_change: Node: readout/dynamics - 'saccadic gating of FlyVis motion readout' (Turner 2022 / Kim 2017 analogy) instead of state remapping. Change: when the crop centre shift exceeds s0 hexals or scale change exceeds r0 per frame (a crop 'saccade'), (a) multiply motion-cell (T4/T5 and downstream) readout weights by g_sac (0 = full suppression) for k frames (k = 1-3 at 30 Hz), (b) keep FlyVis state but do not use it for the object-motion estimate during the window; for small smooth crop following (below s0, r0) apply no cancellation (Fenk 2021 'course-stabilising'), but subtract a forward-model prediction: the response of the same stock FlyVis to the previous frame warped by the known crop transform (static-world expected reafference), computed per cell type, residual = object motion. Variants per rule 6.16: (1) stand without the change; (2) without FlyVis: the same gating applied to DIS flow on the same crops minus crop-transform flow (already the strong control, T4 0.3 px); (3) stock FlyVis with gating + forward-model subtraction; (4) optionally the modernised version. Minimal check (no training, CPU/GPU minutes): rerun the existing technical gate of fly_efference_eye_v1/v2 (same images, 2 px/frame, 8 directions, 12 frames, same T1-T4 thresholds fixed before the run) plus one new condition with a crop jump of >= 3 hexals and a 10% rescale; measure T4 (accumulated error, px) and false transfer T1. Stop conditions (write before running): stop if variant (3) fails T4 <= 12 px or T1 <= 0.1 on the same images, or if (3) is not better than its own ungated version by at least the per-image spread; even if (3) passes, do not claim a FlyVis result unless (3) beats (2) - given DIS already reaches 0.3 px, the realistic expectation is that the fly variant does not beat (2), and then the line should be recorded as 'crop-motion handling solved without FlyVis' and no HOTA run spent. HOTA step (dev35, paired bootstrap) only if (3) beats (2) on the gate.
strongest_objection: The efference-copy literature solves a different problem: suppressing a gaze-stabilising reflex during a voluntary body turn whose kinematics the fly must predict. In our system the eye (crop) motion is set by us and known exactly, so the correct engineering answer is exact coordinate bookkeeping (warp predictions, or compute flow on registered crops), which the project's DIS control already does almost perfectly (T4 0.3 px vs 12.9 px for the remapped fly). Biological cancellation is partial (-5.5 vs +6.4 mV), rotation-only, cell-type-specific and absent for stabilising movements, so copying it cannot outperform exact registration; and none of it touches Z13's real failure (choosing the previous target among similar neighbours and refusing). Using this literature to justify further FlyVis eye-motion work risks a modernisation that is mathematically dominated by a non-FlyVis control.
evidence_strength: Biology [1], [2], [4], [5]: peer-reviewed, whole-cell physiology, moderate-to-strong within the tethered preparation; results partly replicated across labs (Maimon lab [1]-[4]; Schnell lab [5] confirms saccade-related HS hyperpolarisation but only in a subset of HS cells and adds stimulus-driven suppression). Small n per cell type (5-21 cells), tethered saccades 3x slower than free flight; no public analysis code verified. [3], [6], [7]: peer-reviewed but only abstracts checked here (weak verification). [8]: preprint/reviewed preprint, not revised, model not read (weak). [9]: arXiv preprint (later published [uncertain]), single-run ablation without CI (moderate as engineering evidence). Overall for our decision: moderate as a caution (biology does not remap state; cancellation is partial and context-specific), weak as direct support for any specific FlyVis node change.
